## Purpose and primary entry points
MuJoCo is a high-performance articulated-body physics engine with contact simulation. Its core product is a native C/C++ library exposing a C API, compiled models, preallocated runtime state, visualization, and utilities. Public API/data contracts are in `include/mujoco/mujoco.h`, `include/mujoco/mjmodel.h`, and `include/mujoco/mjdata.h`. Native interactive execution starts at `simulate/main.cc`; basic embedding examples start at `sample/basic.cc`.

## Build and package boundary
Top-level CMake assembles the native library, optional renderers, apps, plugins, tests, and bindings: `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/engine/CMakeLists.txt`, `python/mujoco/CMakeLists.txt`. Dependency acquisition/configuration is centralized under `cmake/MujocoDependencies.cmake` and `cmake/third_party_deps/`; important external graphics/UI dependencies include OpenGL/GLAD, GLFW/SDL2, Dear ImGui, and Filament. The project targets native desktop platforms and WebAssembly (`wasm/CMakeLists.txt`).

## Model ingestion and compilation
The user-facing model layer converts MJCF/XML (and supported URDF/assets) into the fixed-layout `mjModel` consumed by simulation. XML parsing, schema-driven reading/writing, and URDF handling live in `src/xml/xml.cc`, `src/xml/xml_native_reader.cc`, and `src/xml/xml_urdf.cc`. Model construction, asset/resource resolution, meshes, composites, flex structures, and virtual filesystems are handled in `src/user/user_model.cc`, `src/user/user_resource.cc`, and `src/user/user_vfs.cc`. This is the major boundary between mutable source descriptions/resources and compiled simulation data.

## Physics runtime pipeline
The engine advances `mjData` against immutable `mjModel`, with low-level memory and callback/plugin integration supporting the runtime. Initialization and orchestration are in `src/engine/engine_init.c` and `src/engine/engine_forward.c`. A typical step flows through kinematics/smooth dynamics and passive forces (`src/engine/engine_core_smooth.c`, `src/engine/engine_passive.c`), collision detection (`src/engine/engine_collision_driver.c`, `src/engine/engine_collision_convex.c`), constraint assembly (`src/engine/engine_core_constraint.c`), and numerical solving (`src/engine/engine_solver.c`). Sensors, inverse dynamics, derivatives, ray queries, sleeping, and islands are adjacent runtime stages.

## Visualization and interactive applications
Visualization derives renderable scene data from model/runtime state, then dispatches to interchangeable rendering backends. Engine visualization preparation is in `src/engine/engine_vis_visualize.c`; classic OpenGL is in `src/render/classic/render_context.c`; the newer Filament backend is rooted at `src/render/filament/mjrfilament.cc`. The `simulate` desktop GUI coordinates GLFW/platform UI, simulation, and rendering through `simulate/simulate.cc` and `simulate/glfw_adapter.cc`. Experimental Studio is a separate richer native/web-oriented application stack: `src/experimental/studio/main.cc`, `src/experimental/studio/app.cc`, `src/experimental/studio/sim/model_holder.cc`.

## Extension and ecosystem surfaces
Plugins extend engine behavior and asset decoding through the public plugin API in `include/mujoco/mjplugin.h` and runtime dispatch in `src/engine/engine_plugin.cc`; reference implementations reside in `plugin/actuator/register.cc` and `plugin/sdf/register.cc`. Python bindings wrap the native library via compiled extensions and Python APIs (`python/mujoco/__init__.py`, `python/mujoco/functions.cc`, `python/mujoco/renderer.py`). MJX is a separate JAX-oriented physics implementation with its own forward/collision/solver path (`mjx/mujoco/mjx/_src/forward.py`, `mjx/mujoco/mjx/_src/collision_driver.py`, `mjx/mujoco/mjx/_src/solver.py`). WebAssembly bindings/demo are generated and exposed from `wasm/codegen/generated/bindings.cc` and `wasm/demo_app/app.ts`; Unity consumes C# bindings/components under `unity/Runtime/Bindings/MjBindings.cs` and `unity/Runtime/Components/MjScene.cs`.
